notes.h: What striking and fielding games share
points: One team bats to score runs (or rounders) while the other bowls or pitches and fields to stop runs and get batters out.
Innings: each team bats in an innings, after which the teams swap roles.
Stance: side-on, feet shoulder-width apart, head still and eyes level.
Grip: hands together at the top of the handle.

notes.h: Cricket drives, cut, pull and glance
points: Drives (straight, on and off) are played to a full ball with a front-foot step towards the ball.
Front-foot drive: head over the ball, high elbow, and a straight bat follow-through.
Back-foot shots are played to shorter balls.
Cut: square on the off side to a short, wide ball.
Pull: horizontal bat to a short ball on the leg side.
Glance: deflects the ball finely on the leg side.
Action in order: run-up, gather, side-on or front-on delivery stride, release, follow-through.
Straight bowling arm, with no throwing.
In cricket the bowling arm must not straighten during delivery (throwing is illegal).

notes.h: Line, length and types of delivery
points: Line: aim at or just outside off stump.
Good length: makes the batter unsure whether to go forward or back.
Medium and fast pace: bowling that uses seam and swing.
Spin: off-spin and leg-spin, which turn the ball off the pitch.
Close fielding (slips, short leg): low, ready, with soft hands.
Deep fielding (boundary): take a long barrier to stop the ball.
Deep fielding: attack the ball and make a flat throw to the keeper.

notes.h: Catching and throwing in softball and rounders
points: Catching: two-handed, with the hands forming a cup or basket and giving with the ball.
Throwing: overarm, from a side-on stance, stepping towards the target.
Stance: side-on, with the eyes on the ball.
Swing: level through the ball, with a full follow-through.
After the hit, the batter runs to the next post or base.

notes.h: Pitching and bowling in softball and rounders
points: Rounders bowling is underarm.
In rounders the ball must pass between the batter's head and knee on the batting side.
Variations: pace, swerve and spin.
Line and length: the ball is pitched to a consistent line and length.

notes.h: Fielding positions in softball and rounders
points: Rounders positions: backstop, bowler, and first to fourth post fielders.
Softball positions: basemen, with deep fielders covering the outfield.
Fielding on base: stretch to catch the ball with a foot on the base.
Deep fielders back up: move behind the fielder throwing the ball, so that a missed or overthrown ball can be stopped.
Runs: batters run between the wickets to score.
Boundaries: 4 runs when the ball crosses the boundary along the ground, and 6 when it crosses on the full.
Dismissals: bowled, caught, run out, LBW and stumped.
Rounders: a rounder is scored by reaching fourth post.
Rounders: a batter is out if caught, if a post is stumped before they reach it, or if they overtake another batter.
Softball: runs are scored for reaching home.
Softball: three outs end the innings.
Batting into gaps: placing the ball where fielders cannot reach it.
Running calls between wickets or posts: yes, no or wait.
Fielding placement is set for the batter and for the bowler.
Bowling to the field that has been set.

notes.h: Safety in striking and fielding games
points: Cricket protective equipment: helmet, pads, gloves and box.
A hard ball creates a danger zone, so players must stay alert to where it is travelling.
Batters drop the bat, never throw it.
Fielders call for catches so that team-mates do not collide.

A drive in which the batter steps the front foot towards a full ball, keeping the head over it.
A square shot on the off side played to a short, wide ball.
A horizontal-bat shot played to a short ball on the leg side.
A shot that deflects the ball finely on the leg side.
The direction of the bowler's delivery, aimed at or just outside off stump.
How far down the pitch the ball lands, with a good length making the batter unsure whether to go forward or back.
The edge of the cricket field, where a ball that reaches it scores 4 or 6.
A way of getting a batter out, such as bowled, caught, run out, LBW or stumped.
The score in rounders gained by a batter who reaches fourth post.
The rounders fielder positioned behind the batter.
Softball fielders who guard the bases.
Moving behind a fielder who is throwing, so that a missed or overthrown ball can be stopped.

questions.prompt: Describe the front-foot drive in cricket and explain how line and length affect the batter's choice of shot.
questions.model: Front-foot drive: the batter steps the front foot towards the pitch of a full ball, keeps the head over the ball with the eyes on it, and drives with a high elbow, finishing with a straight bat follow-through. Line and length: the bowler aims at or just outside off stump, which is the line the batter must judge. A good length makes the batter unsure whether to go forward or back, so the batter has to read the length early. A full ball suits the front-foot drive, while a shorter ball calls for a back-foot shot such as the cut, pull or glance.

questions.prompt: Describe how to catch and throw a ball in rounders or softball.
questions.model: Catch: use two hands, with the hands forming a cup or basket, and give with the ball as it arrives so that it is cushioned. Throw: use an overarm throw from a side-on stance, stepping towards the target as the ball is released.
